newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up on expected export deals.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up on expected export deals.

text.p: The won finished stronger versus the dollar on Thursday as expectations of large month-end export deals and dollar inflow of funds from depository receipt issues spurred buying for the local currency, dealers said.
The won closed at a day high of 828.40 after opening at 829.50. It touched a low of 829.80.
Dealers said export deals were expected to pour in mostly on Friday and Saturday.
Investors anticipated strong dollar sales by Cho Hung Bank, which issued $180 million worth of global depository receipts (GDR) in London overnight.
Traders expect the won to remain strong on Friday, with trading ranging from 827.70 to 829.20. The central bank set the base mid-rate at 828.80 for Friday against 829.90 today.
